instruction: My daughter sent me a message yesterday on phone about an app account creation. Please do as per her message. Use password j7}yl^6 for the new account.
notes: The daughter's text (found via phone.search_contacts(relationship=daughter) then phone.search_text_messages(phone_number=...)) says an account was already created for the supervisor on some app with her email, and asks her to verify it and set a password. The evaluation confirms this: one existing <app>.User record is updated (verified=True, password=j7}yl^6) and gmail receives 'Account Verficiation Code', 'Password Reset Code' and 'Password Changed' emails, which is exactly the trace of send_verification_code -> verify_account -> send_password_reset_code -> reset_password. The target app is only known at runtime from the message; it is modeled with the constant `spotify` as a stand-in, and the four account actions should be issued against the app named in the message (amazon, file_system, simple_note, splitwise, spotify, todoist and venmo all expose the identical send_verification_code/verify_account/send_password_reset_code/reset_password APIs). No login to the target app is needed (or possible) since its password is unknown. Codes are read from gmail by searching the inbox and then showing the thread; the verification/reset code emails only exist after the corresponding send call (thread-exists). Verification and password reset are not ordered relative to each other since both orders are valid. The task asks no question, so supervisor-complete-task carries only task-record parameters (the account email and new password) and no answer.
